verifications.claim: The class must share common questions of law or fact.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the existence of questions common to the class'; R8: 'Commonality. The case involves questions of law or fact common to all class members.'; R12: 'claims of the class members contain questions of law or fact in common'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches Rule 23(a)(2) prerequisite for commonality stated in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: The class is too large for individual lawsuits to be practical.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'numerousness of the class making joinder of the members impracticable'; R3: 'too many plaintiffs to sue individually in a practical way'; R8: 'so many class members that it's impracticable to join them'
verifications.reasoning: Precisely describes numerosity requirement under Rule 23(a)(1).

verifications.claim: A court must officially certify the group as a class.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the court to determine... whether an action brought as a class action is to be so maintained'; R3: 'Seek class certification from the appropriate court'; R8: 'it must be certified by a court'; R12: 'before the lawsuit can proceed as a class action'
verifications.reasoning: Court certification is a standard requirement explicitly stated across sources.

verifications.claim: Potential members can "opt out" to retain the right to sue individually.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the right of each member to be excluded from the class upon his request'; R8: 'opt out of the class action... free to file their own lawsuit'
verifications.reasoning: Directly describes opt-out right for Rule 23(b)(3) classes in certification notices.
